Two Words in Ulysses

A note written for the book-links test suite.

Readers of Ulysses soon learn to watch for two words. The first is "parallax", which Leopold
Bloom half remembers from a popular astronomy book and turns over all day without quite
understanding it. The second is "metempsychosis", which Molly Bloom stumbles on in a novel and
asks her husband to explain. Both words return again and again, and a later novel that uses
either of them prominently is very likely nodding at Joyce.

The book also leans on Shakespeare. Stephen Dedalus carries Hamlet with him through the day, and
his theory of the play, of fathers, sons and ghosts, is the substance of the library episode.
The note also mentions an unnamed pamphlet that is not in any collection.
